subject: ventures/home-inspection-fee-calculator
professional: an independent licensed home inspector who sets their own fee schedule; they check first whether the time model matches a real job (on-site hours, report-writing hours, drive time), whether square-footage tiers and the age/foundation premiums look like their own schedule, how add-ons (radon, sewer scope, WDO, mold, pool) are priced, and whether the fee clears E&O, software and agreement costs at their weekly volume

evidence.correctness: Independent Python model (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/06e0cb4f-6864-5ca6-b547-e6e7d6dd4a2d/scratchpad/hi/model.py) written from the README/article description with Decimal arithmetic (base hours = max(1.25, sqft/800), +0.25 h per story above one, crawl +0.5 / basement +0.25, age bands 10/25/60 y, rush on labor only, miles x rate, add-ons, overhead, price = cost/(1-margin)), compared with node runs of calculateQuote (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/06e0cb4f-6864-5ca6-b547-e6e7d6dd4a2d/scratchpad/hi/run.mjs) and with the page in headless Chrome (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/06e0cb4f-6864-5ca6-b547-e6e7d6dd4a2d/scratchpad/hi/pw.py). Defaults: 3.75 h, cost 424.00, price 565.33, profit 141.33 in all three. How-to worked example (2,800 sf, crawl, 45 y, 30 mi, 95/h, rush, radon + sewer): 4.75 h, rush 67.69, cost 899.94, price 1,199.92, profit 299.98 in all three; weekly 5 x 299.98 = 1,499.90, gap 500.10, 2 more jobs. vs-flat pair: 2.5 h / 398.67 and 4.5 h / 665.33 (4.5/2.5 = 1.8). Market cross-check: the 2.5 h for 2,000 sf matches the 2-3 h on-site range in HomeGauge/HomeLight guides, and the slab case's 398.67 sits inside the 75-500 quoted for 2,000 sf (Angi lists 75-400 for 2,000-2,500 sf). Not 4: the 'about $137.69/hr all-in' line is labor rate + profit/hour, not revenue per on-site hour (565.33/3.75 = 150.76), and add-on 'fees' are grossed up by the margin (radon $150 adds $200.00 to the price).
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README and page list was exercised in headless Chrome: square footage, stories, three foundation types, age, travel, hourly rate, rush premium on labor only, four add-ons with editable fees, overhead, margin, weekly income check (default 140 x 5 vs 2,000: $700.00, $1300.00 gap, 10 more), local draft save ('Restored your last job from this browser.' after reload), Reset to defaults (back to 2,000 sf / $565.33), usage opt-out, links to the three articles (200) and LICENSE. No TODOs or stubs; no console errors; no horizontal scroll at 375 px (scrollWidth 375).
evidence.verification: cd ventures/home-inspection-fee-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 40 tests, 40 pass, 0 fail. Eight mutations through platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on calc.mjs: six caught (age >=60 -> >60, base hours per sf, extra-story count, margin -> markup, effective hourly formula, basement hours), two survived: MIN_BASE_HOURS 1.25 -> 1.0 (the small-home floor that sets every condo price is untested) and meetsTarget gap <= 0 -> < 0 (the exactly-on-goal boundary). The article numbers 1,199.92, 398.67 and 665.33 are pinned by page.test.mjs and vs-a-flat test; the expected values are the author's own arithmetic, matched here by an independent model.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (164 lines), index.html module script (114-224), usage.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Pure, small, validated core with readable errors (a '1,200' or blank square footage shows 'Square footage must be a positive number.'). Defects: a blank add-on fee with the add-on ticked becomes $0 silently (Number('') = 0; the page dropped from $1199.92 to $999.92 with no error), blank overhead likewise; weeklyIncomeGap accepts negative inspections (-3 jobs -> -$1200.00 and '8' more); money() has no thousands separator ('$1300.00'); the weekly 'profit per inspection' is a hard-coded 140, not linked to the quote's profit.
evidence.claims: All dollar and hour figures on the how-to, vs-flat and index pages match the independent model. Disclaimer present on index, README and all three articles (loaded in Chrome); privacy claim backed (no fetch/beacon; usage.mjs is localStorage only), though the page lists two counted events while index.html:211 also records 'sponsor_link_clicked'. Unbacked or contradicted: (1) README, index meta/lede/FAQ and both comparison pages say add-ons are priced 'at their own flat fee', but calc.mjs:126-127 puts them in cost and divides by (1 - margin), so a $150 radon fee adds $200 to the quote; (2) vs-flat:66 and :92 say 'the actual on-site time differs by 80%', which is the model's uncited constants, not measured time; (3) the time premiums are presented as 'the specifics that actually drive on-site time' with no source for 0.00125 h/sf, 0.25 h/story, 0.5 h crawl or the age bands. Served page not checked: marisstella.app is outside this session's allowed hosts (CONNECT 403), so source llms.txt github.io URLs are not filed (rewritten at deploy).
evidence.fitness: Walked an inspector's quote: 2,800 sf two-story crawlspace, 45 years, radon + sewer, same-day report. The tool gives a defensible line-item quote quickly. Gaps an inspector hits in the first hour: labor is on-site hours only, so report writing (commonly 1-2+ h per job) and drive time are unpaid unless folded into the hourly rate; no square-footage tier table, which is how inspectors publish fees; no pool/spa, outbuilding, condo/multi-unit, re-inspection or ancillary like well/septic/thermal add-ons; no annual break-even (E&O, software, agreements, association dues) at a weekly volume, only a flat $35 overhead. A sibling venture (home-inspection-business-profit-calculator, linked at index.html:108) covers report hours and fixed cost, which softens but does not close the gap here.
evidence.domain: Compared with published practice: on-site time 2-3 h for 2,000 sf (HomeGauge, HomeLight, Spectora guides) matches the 2.5 h base; one guide's +30 min per 500 sf is close to the tool's 0.00125 h/sf (37.5 min per 500 sf). Departures: (a) pricing only on-site hours omits report time, which practitioners treat as a large share of a job; (b) add-on fees are marked up by the job margin, so retail-looking defaults (radon 150, sewer 175, WDO 90, mold 125) become 200/233/120/167 in the price; (c) mileage default 0.70 is the IRS 2025 rate, the 2026 rate is 72.5 cents (IR-2025-128; secondary sources report 76 cents from July 2026), uncited and stale; (d) no source for the foundation, story or age premiums; (e) industry fee schedules are square-footage tiers with add-on menus, not hourly; the tool does not output one. The default crawl/2-story/25-y quote of $565.33 sits above Angi's $275-400 band for 2,000-2,500 sf, which is defensible as a floor but not compared on the page.

defects.what: Add-on fees are added to cost and grossed up by the target margin, so a ticked $150 radon test adds $200.00 to the quote (sewer 175 -> 233.33), while the README, index lede/FAQ and both comparison pages say add-ons are priced 'at their own flat fee'.
Labor is on-site hours only; report-writing time and drive time are never priced, though practitioners count report time as a large share of each job. Only mileage is charged for travel.

Two seeded mutations survive: MIN_BASE_HOURS 1.25 -> 1.0 (the small-home floor) and the weekly goal boundary gap <= 0 -> < 0; no test prices a home under 1,000 sf or a week that lands exactly on the goal.

Time constants (0.00125 h/sf, 0.25 h/story, 0.5 h crawl, 0.25 h basement, age bands) and add-on/overhead defaults are uncited; the default mileage rate 0.70 is the IRS 2025 rate (2026 is 72.5 cents, IR-2025-128).
'the actual on-site time differs by 80%' states the model's uncited estimate as measured time.
The 'about $X/hr all-in' line is base rate plus profit per on-site hour ($137.69 on defaults), not revenue per hour ($150.76); 'all-in' misdescribes it and add-on margin inflates it.
Blank add-on fee (with the add-on ticked) or blank overhead silently becomes $0; weeklyIncomeGap accepts negative bookings (-3 -> '8' more); money() prints $1300.00 with no thousands separator.
Privacy section lists the counted events as quote-priced and weekly-goal-check, but the page also records sponsor_link_clicked.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: an independent model reproduces the defaults, the how-to worked example, the vs-flat pair and the weekly check to the cent, in node and on the page in headless Chrome, and the 2.5 h / $398.67 easy case sits inside published on-site-time and price ranges. It does not meet the bar. Claims fall to 2 because every page says add-ons are priced 'at their own flat fee' while the code grosses them up by the margin (a $150 radon test adds $200), and an 80% 'actual' time gap rests on uncited constants. Verification is 2: two of eight seeded mutations survive, including the small-home minimum. For an inspector the method misses report-writing and drive hours, square-footage tiers and common add-ons such as pool or outbuildings, and the mileage default is last year's IRS rate.
